name: MQF (Mixed-counters Quotient Filter)
workload: Query time for 35 million existing real k-mers looked up in MQF filters loaded to 60%, 70%, 80% and 90% capacity, with MQF's per-key 'label' feature used as a minimal perfect hash function and compared against BBHash-style MPHFs
claimed_speedup: ~10-fold faster query time than BBHash (MPHFs), with MQF query time reported as invariable across load factors (paper Additional file 1, Figure S6; abstract states "the labels serve as a minimal perfect hash function but are ~10 fold faster than BBhash")
hardware: AWS t3.large instance (2 vCPUs, 8GB RAM), Ubuntu Server 18.04 (exact CPU model not specified; burstable cloud instance type)
stars_or_usage: 12 stars; published in BMC Bioinformatics 22:71 (2021), used in k-mer/genomics counting pipelines from the dib-lab group
tradeoffs: MQF is fundamentally a dynamic counting/labeling quotient filter (supports insert/remove/resize/merge) rather than a pure static MPHF like BBHash, so the 'perfect hash' behavior is one feature (label lookup) of a broader data structure, not a drop-in MPHF replacement; a buffered/disk-backed variant trades speed for memory; comparison hardware is a shared/burstable cloud VM rather than a dedicated bare-metal benchmark box
caveats: Speedup is reported as an aggregate '~10 fold' claim tied to a supplementary figure (Additional file 1, Fig. S6) rather than a detailed per-configuration numeric table; exact CPU model and compiler/optimization flags are not stated, so this is capped at Tier B despite being a peer-reviewed journal paper; the GitHub project has not been updated since October 2023
found_via: WebSearch: 'MQF minimal perfect hash function k-mer "10 fold faster" BBHash github' -> dib-lab/MQF; cross-checked against BMC Bioinformatics paper via PMC (PMC7885209)

verification.tier_reason: The paper (BMC Bioinformatics 22:71) says MQF block labels are ~10x faster than BBHash; Supplementary Fig. S6 shows about 300 ms for MQF vs about 3,100-3,550 ms for BBHash over 35M queries. The only harness for that figure is taggingTest.cpp in dib-lab/2020-paper-mqf-benchmarks (the same file is on the MQF 'benchmark' branch). It builds the MQF through Benchmark_Utils_Script/countingStructure.hpp with qf_init(..., blocksLabelSize=0, ...), so itemOrder() in gqf.cpp returns 0 immediately at `if(qf->metadata->BlockLabel_bits!=32) return 0;` and never searches the filter. That leaves no valid numbers against the baseline.
verification.notes: Category check as requested: MQF is not an MPHF. Its only comparison against a listed baseline for this category is BBHash in Fig. S6, and the published code for that figure never runs the MQF lookup (blocksLabelSize=0 in every version of countingStructure.hpp I checked, back to 2019). I cannot rule out an unpublished local change, but the paper says all experiment code is in that repo. Metadata matches gh: BSD-3-Clause, 12 stars, last commit 2023-10-01, stale.
verification.reject_reason: other: MQF is a counting quotient filter, not an MPHF, and its only comparison against a listed baseline (BBHash, Fig. S6) is invalid because the published harness never performs the MQF lookup
